title: The Bakery of Sandpiper Point
premise: Wendell Vasquez, a jaded wedding planner nursing a decade-old betrayal, has been exchanging anonymous letters with a stranger through the mailbox of his late grandmother's bakery in Sandpiper Point. When the letter writer — estate lawyer Priya Raghavan, who inherited the bakery's deed — arrives to claim the building, Wendell discovers she's been the voice behind every letter, and that her firm's client, a resort developer, intends to demolish the bakery for a vineyard wedding venue. As they collaborate to save the bakery and stage the vineyard's first harvest festival, Wendell must choose between the safe, transactional love he's perfected and the whole-hearted risk Priya demands. The story ends with Wendell surrendering his controlling grip, Priya walking away from the corrupt firm that raised her, and the two of them reopening the bakery together on the morning of the first harvest.
about_author: Mara Oyelaran is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in small coastal towns where food and memory intertwine. She lives on the Atlantic seaboard with her family and an unreasonable number of sourdough starters.

chapters.title: The Mailbox at the End of the Pier
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He plans a flawless wedding for clients who despise each other, then retreats to his grandmother's shuttered bakery to drop a letter in the old mailbox — a ritual he's kept for ten years. The beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She arrives in Sandpiper Point carrying a deed to the bakery and instructions from her firm's client, Meridian Resorts, to secure the property. Reading a decade of returned letters in her car, she realizes she wrote every reply. The beat: guilt surfacing under professional armor.

chapters.title: Neighbor, Unexpected
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Priya moves into the cottage next door and introduces herself as the bakery's new owner. Wendell recognizes her handwriting from the letters and says nothing, testing whether she'll confess. The beat: wary fascination.

chapters.title: What the Deed Says
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She reviews the fine print: Meridian plans a vineyard wedding venue where the bakery stands, and her signature triggers demolition. She drafts a resignation she doesn't send. The beat: complicity versus conscience.

chapters.title: Flour and Fine Print
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wendell offers to help her 'assess' the bakery, and they bake his grandmother's bread together; flour-dusted and laughing, they nearly cross a line before a Meridian surveyor interrupts. The beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Letters I Never Sent
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Wendell confronts her with the letters; she admits she answered them as a law clerk who fell for a stranger's grief and never had the courage to sign her name. The beat: raw confession, trust cracked but alive.

chapters.title: Harvest Deadline
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Meridian's demolition notice gives them until the vineyard's first harvest, six weeks out. Wendell proposes they save the bakery by proving it's a living business — and that Priya fight her own firm. The beat: resolve kindled.

chapters.title: Pieces of a Heart on Loan
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Wendell, terrified of full commitment, offers her 'pieces' of himself — weekends, no future. She refuses the ration, echoing her own history of half-measures at the firm. The beat: the cost of guarded love.

chapters.title: The Partner's Handshake
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Her mentor, Marcus Hale, offers her partnership if she closes the bakery deal quietly, revealing the firm buried evidence that Wendell's grandmother was defrauded of the deed. The beat: temptation dressed as reward.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the bakery's cellar, Wendell and Priya find his grandmother's ledgers proving the fraudulent 1998 transfer. Grief and anger fuse into purpose. The beat: the past weaponized for the future.

chapters.title: A Town Divided
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At a town meeting, Meridian promises jobs while Wendell makes an impassioned case for the bakery; neighbors split, and an old friend of his grandmother testifies about the fraud. The beat: community stakes raised, first public victory.

chapters.title: The Vineyard Tour
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Meridian courts Wendell personally, offering him the venue-planning contract of a lifetime — his name on every brochure. He almost signs before seeing Priya's face in the crowd. The beat: power's seduction tested.

chapters.title: What I'd Burn
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya copies the fraud file and mails it to the county clerk, knowing it ends her career. Marcus warns her that loyalty is the only currency that matters. The beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Six Weeks of Almost
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A montage of the bakery's restoration: paint, ovens, festival plans, stolen kisses. But Wendell still withholds his full history — the wedding he abandoned at the altar and the fiancée he wronged. The beat: warmth shadowed by secrets.

chapters.title: The Groom Who Ran
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya learns Wendell's fiancée left him at the altar, not the reverse — his whole cynicism is built on a shame that isn't his. She demands he stop editing his own story. The beat: identity confronted.

chapters.title: Meridian Moves
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Meridian files an emergency injunction using a clause Priya's firm inserted years ago; the harvest festival permit is revoked and Marcus offers to make it vanish — if Priya returns and destroys the ledger. The beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Letter That Started Everything
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wendell finds the first letter he ever wrote, and Priya's unsent reply from ten years ago, in which she almost came to find him. They finally speak plainly about timing, fear, and the years lost to caution. The beat: full emotional exposure.

chapters.title: Hearing Day
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. At the county hearing, Priya testifies against her own firm, presenting the ledger and the fraud file. Marcus attempts to discredit her; the town and Wendell stand with her. The beat: climax of the external plot — courage over corruption.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The injunction falls, and the vineyard's first harvest festival becomes the bakery's reopening — bread and wine, the whole town, Wendell planning a celebration he finally believes in. The beat: joy earned, the theme of inheritance redeemed.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wendell gives Priya a letter — signed, dated, addressed to her by name — asking for the whole-hearted love he once rationed. She answers with her own unsent letter from a decade ago. The beat: the romantic climax.

chapters.title: Partnership of a Different Kind
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Marcus is disbarred; Priya declines a bigger firm's offer to instead become the bakery's co-owner and the town's pro bono counsel. The beat: power redefined as stewardship.

chapters.title: Open at Six
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Opening morning at the Bakery of Sandpiper Point: the two of them, the mailbox restored, a new letter from a stranger waiting inside. Wendell answers it — signed this time. The beat: the cycle of connection renewed, ending on warmth.
